source_title: Jio posts about 14% profit rise in first results since blockbuster debut - Business Standard
source_excerpt: Jio Platforms Ltd (JPL), the parent company of India’s largest telecom-services provider Reliance Jio, on Friday reported a net profit of ₹8,389 crore for July-September 2026-27 in its first earnings report after its blockbuster market listing earlier this week. Net profit was up 13.7 per cent from ₹7,379 crore in the same period last financial year. Revenues rose 11.4 per cent to ₹40,475 crore from ₹36,332 crore the same quarter last year. In the previous quarter, profits were ₹7,764 crore and revenues ₹39,173 crore.The company raised ₹30,188 crore in what is India’s largest initial public offering. “We were raising ₹30,000 crore-odd, and we saw demand of over ₹7.5 trillion. We saw every investor category broken, starting from QIB (qualified institutional buyers) to small HNI (high net worth), big HNI, retail, and all the various shareholders, employees, all of the categories were broken,” said Akash Ambani, managing director, JPL, at the analyst call following the results. The top executive at India’s second-largest company by market capitalisation said that JPL’s IPO numbers came at a time when the Indian markets had seen outflows of more than ₹48,000 crore, led by foreign portfolio investors. “In a market situation like that, (we are) very proud that the people (are) realising (what) business we’ve built ... we put in extremely hard work over the last 10 years to build this business, and we’ll continue to do so,” Ambani noted, adding, the IPO was a new milestone, and that the company would move on from here. “We believe that you know the value that we can create over the next decade or so is even more than what we have done in our first decade, and we’ll continue to aspire to that perspective,” he said.Quarterly earnings before interest tax, depreciation and amortisation climbed 16.6 per cent year-on-year to ₹21,879 crore. The 250-basis point rise in margins was driven by revenue growth and operating leverage. Jio reported average revenue per user (Arpu), a monthly metric of profitability of a telecom services provider, at ₹218.8, marginally up from ₹215.6 in Q1FY27. However, year-on-year, Arpu was up 3.5 per cent, from ₹211.4, on the back of promotional schemes for fixed broadband customers and increased usage. “We warmly welcome our new shareholders to the Jio Platforms family as we enter a new era as a listed company. This quarter’s results continue to reflect the strength of our 5G network, and the growing reach of our broadband and digital services,” Ambani said in a statement to the exchanges. The company said in its statement to the stock exchanges that ₹27,500 crore from the net proceeds from the IPO has been used to prepay, in full or in part, the principal amount outstanding of the external commercial borrowing of Reliance Jio Infocomm Ltd, a material subsidiary of JPL, and the balance amount would be for general corporate purposes.JPL’s net debt reduced by 78.6 per cent to ₹8,822 crore from ₹41,161 crore in Q2FY26. Debt reduced quarter-on-quarter by 7.5 per cent from ₹9,539 crore in Q1FY27. Finance costs rose 40.3 per cent to ₹3,009 crore, up from ₹2,145 crore in Q2FY26.Reliance Jio ended September 2026 with 542.4 million users, including 300 million 5G subscribers. The carrier added 9.1 million subscribers during the quarter. Jio’s 5G data traffic in the fourth quarter reached 71.3 billion gigabytes, while total voice traffic rose 1.3 per cent to 1.52 trillion minutes. It added 66 million 5G customers over the last 12 months, and 15 million over the past quarter. Customer engagement also remains robust with data consumption at 44.2 GB per month, higher than 38.7 GB per month in the same period last year. Fixed broadband subscribers as of September 2026 stood at 30 million with about 7.3 million additions over the last 12 months. Jio AirFiber had over 15.1 million subscribers, driving more than 75 per cent of the fixed broadband additions during the last 12 months, the company said.“Ahead of the curve investment on next generation technologies has been the foundation of Jio’s success over the past decade. We would continue to build our capabilities across satellite communications, 6G intellectual property and AI embedded in our core voice and data services as we create lasting value for all our stakeholders,” Ambani added.He elaborated the company’s strategy, noting that it was unlike a traditional telecom services provider owing largely to its proprietary technology with integrated 4G, 5G stack, unlicensed broadband radio (UBR) and now fixed wireless becoming 50 per cent of its base. He added that Jio would double down on offers to the enterprise because it would be a major growth opportunity, with India having 350,000 lease lines. On expanding internationally, Ambani said that the company would be “very selective” about the markets that it would go to. “We will not be selling our proprietary stacks as a hardware commission … What we imagine the business model here to be is to be actually managed service partner with our customers. It’s not going to be a heavy capex rollout. You won’t see us going and putting up towers and fiber and infrastructure only. But this is something that we think that will be enabled because of the only proprietary stack that we have," he added. Stating the company’s competitive advantage — owing to full-stack technology across seven layers, deep engineering and proprietary IP contribution — Ambani said Jio had multiple growth engines across mobility, home, enterprise, and international. “We are the ones that have a clear path of growth and profitability improving with a very strong balance sheet, even before the IPO proceeds come to us,” he added.
